reviewChoiceGroups.title: Architecture disposition
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose how to handle the platform shell architecture findings.

options.label: Single branch, no CSS shell selection
options.description: Proceed with React deciding one mounted shell and remove CSS breakpoint rules that hide the selected shell.
options.rationale: This matches the platform-not-viewport requirement and fixes the desktop-narrow blank UI risk.

options.label: CSS breakpoint selection
options.description: Let media queries continue to choose or hide mobile/desktop shells.
options.rationale: This is responsive-design friendly but directly contradicts the selected platform rule.

options.label: Layout service redesign
options.description: Stop and build a broader layout service with override/tablet logic.
options.rationale: Use only if the team wants to expand scope beyond the current platform-detector plan.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Code quality stance
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose the code organization standard for the layout change.

options.label: Pure detector + local shells
options.description: Keep isMobileBrowserPlatform pure, keep shell functions local in App until they grow, and keep shared screens shared.
options.rationale: This gives strong testability without over-extracting a small one-bit decision.

options.label: Extract shells now
options.description: Create separate MobileShell and DesktopShell files immediately.
options.rationale: Reasonable if App.tsx grows, but not necessary for this implementation pass.

options.label: Inline platform in App
options.description: Remove the detector module and check navigator directly inside App.tsx.
options.rationale: Smallest code footprint, but much worse unit-testability and future maintainability.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Validation requirement
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose the runtime UI validation gate before accepting this plan.

options.label: Matrix + two full flows
options.description: Add desktop-wide, desktop-narrow, mobile-phone, and mobile-wide shell tests, plus full mobile and desktop user flows with screenshots.
options.rationale: This directly proves platform-versus-viewport behavior while keeping runtime cost controlled.

options.label: Two flows only
options.description: Keep one mobile and one desktop flow without cross-checking narrow/wide platform behavior.
options.rationale: Faster, but misses the exact regression risk found in the review: CSS breakpoint shell selection.

options.label: Unit tests only
options.description: Rely on detector unit tests and skip expanded Playwright runtime coverage.
options.rationale: Insufficient because shell visibility and CSS can still violate the detector contract at runtime.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Performance and risk response
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose how to address platform ambiguity, CSS risk, and test artifacts.

options.label: Document UI-only + reset DB
options.description: Document detector caveats, keep it UI-only, reset IndexedDB per scenario, and use synthetic screenshots.
options.rationale: This handles known UA and local-data risks without adding product scope.

options.label: Add layout override now
options.description: Add a user-facing/persisted switch to force mobile or desktop.
options.rationale: Mitigates UA ambiguity, but introduces new UI, state, persistence, and tests.

options.label: Accept untested ambiguity
options.description: Ship platform detection with no matrix and no CSS shell-selection cleanup.
options.rationale: Fastest path, but leaves the current critical desktop-narrow failure mode open.

reviewChoiceGroups.title: Final disposition
reviewChoiceGroups.prompt: Choose the final disposition for the revised platform-layout plan.

options.label: Approve with guardrails
options.description: Implement the plan after removing CSS shell selection and adding the platform/viewport Playwright matrix.
options.rationale: The plan is sound, but current nearby CSS and E2E coverage are not yet aligned with it.

options.label: Request changes first
options.description: Revise the plan to explicitly call out CSS cleanup, test projects, and IndexedDB reset helpers before coding.
options.rationale: Choose this if the written plan must be fully precise before implementation continues.

options.label: Reject platform rule
options.description: Reject platform detection and redesign around responsive viewport-based layout.
options.rationale: Better general UX, but conflicts with the explicit selected requirement.
